newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russia's LUKoil plans convertible bond.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia's LUKoil plans convertible bond.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company, NK LUKoil, in the middle of an aggressive expansion at home and abroad, said on Thursday it planned a new convertible bond issue this year to help finance its investments.
The new bond is the latest stage in the star company's massive, multi-faceted funding programme.

This week LUKoil privately placed a $125 million bond with international institutions, and last month shareholders authorised the issue of 10 million preferred shares while the company said it was working on an oil-backed bond issue.
"A (convertible) issue is planned, and further issues are being worked on. By the end of this year would be realistic," LUKoil Vice-President Nikolai Tsvetkov told a news conference.
"We are planning securities issues, starting with international markets. We are studying the possibility of attracting private capital to invest in our internal projects."

Tsvetkov said it was premature to discuss the terms of the new bond, but said LUKoil could attract more favourable conditions now that it had received a credit rating. It was rated BB minus by Standard and Poor's this month.

A $200 million convertible bond was oversubscribed in April, and LUKoil made two other convertible issues in 1995, mainly bought up by U.S. oil company Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO), which ended up with 7.99 percent of LUKoil as a result.
The company is already largely privatised, but wants to push back the planned sale of a 15 percent government stake to next year, when an audit to international standards will be ready.

Proceeds from the sale will be shared by the cash-strapped government and LUKoil, which wants to place the shares with foreign investors by issuing level-three American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), share look-alikes traded in the U.S.
Tsvetkov said LUKoil was also holding back on issuing a Eurobond until the international figures, being prepared by KPMG, are ready at the end of this year or early in 1998.

LUKoil, which says it is the world's largest private oil company in terms of crude oil reserves, owning some 10.5 billion barrels in Russia alone, is one of a handful of Russian oil companies whose output is rising.
Its exports of oil products are soaring as it upgrades and expands refinery operations.
LUKoil is aggressively building up its foreign exploration portfolio and is working on increasing its refining capacity, as well as moving into other downstream activities such as gas stations.
It signed deals worth a total of $3 billion with Azerbaijan this month to develop oilfields in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea, and has plans for more.
Oil from the region, which could one day rival the Persian Gulf in terms of output, will flow initially through Russia.

LUKoil also has a stake in Kazakhstan's huge Tengiz field through its LUKArco venture with ARCO, and is part of the international consortium building a major pipeline from Kazakhstan to the Black Sea.
U.S. bank Chase Manhattan is advising LUKoil on its plans to issue bonds backed by oil exports from the Caspian, Tsvetkov said.
At 1300 GMT, LUKoil, whose share price has roughly doubled, this year, was $20.70 on the Russian Trading System, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
